experiences.name: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise
experiences.description: Embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden boat (dhoni) decorated with flowers and candles for a private sunset cruise with your partner. Enjoy champagne, fresh tropical fruits, and canapés while watching the sky turn shades of gold and pink over the Indian Ocean. A quintessential romantic honeymoon experience unique to the Maldives.
experiences.location: North Malé Atoll, around Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Coral Garden Snorkeling Safari
experiences.description: Explore some of the most vibrant coral reefs in the world on a guided snorkeling safari. Drift through kaleidoscopic coral gardens teeming with sea turtles, reef sharks, manta rays, and thousands of tropical fish. A professional guide leads you to three different snorkeling spots across the atoll, including a famous manta ray cleaning station.
experiences.location: Hanifaru Bay, Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve

experiences.name: Underwater Restaurant Dinner for Two
experiences.description: Dine in an extraordinary all-glass underwater restaurant surrounded by the living ocean. Enjoy a curated five-course fine dining menu featuring fresh Maldivian lobster, tuna sashimi, and decadent desserts while nurse sharks and colorful reef fish glide past your table. An unforgettable luxury dining experience perfect for honeymooners.
experiences.location: Ithaa Undersea Restaurant, Conrad Maldives Rangali Island, South Ari Atoll

experiences.name: Bioluminescent Beach Night Walk
experiences.description: After dark, witness the magical natural phenomenon of bioluminescent plankton lighting up the shoreline in electric blue as waves wash ashore. Walk hand-in-hand along the beach as the water glows beneath your feet. Combine this with a private stargazing session guided by a resort astronomer using high-powered telescopes under some of the clearest skies on Earth.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class & Local Island Cultural Tour
experiences.description: Visit a local inhabited island to experience authentic Maldivian culture beyond the resort bubble. Tour a traditional fishing village, visit a local mosque, and browse handcrafted lacquerware at a artisan workshop. Then join a hands-on cooking class learning to prepare classic dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut), garudhiya fish soup, and coconut roshi flatbread using fresh local ingredients.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Maldives
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.location: North Malé Atoll, around Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class & Local Island Cultural Tour
experiences.description: Visit a local inhabited island to experience authentic Maldivian culture beyond the resort bubble. Tour a traditional fishing village, visit a local mosque, and browse handcrafted lacquerware at a artisan workshop. Then join a hands-on cooking class learning to prepare classic dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut), garudhiya fish soup, and coconut roshi flatbread using fresh local ingredients.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage. Arrange a budget speedboat or shared dhoni transfer to North Malé Atoll (book in advance to save costs vs. private transfers). Check in to your boutique guesthouse near Veligandu/Baros area. Freshen up and explore the property, settle into your room, and get oriented with the island layout.
day_by_day.evening: Take a slow sunset stroll along the beach or jetty — your first golden Maldivian sunset. Enjoy a welcome drink at the guesthouse (often complimentary). Dine at the guesthouse restaurant or a nearby local café for an easy, relaxed first night.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport before boarding transfer
meals.lunch: Light meal or snacks purchased at the airport or convenience store near the guesthouse on arrival
meals.dinner: Guesthouse restaurant or nearby local café — try Mas Huni (tuna and coconut) or Garudhiya (tuna broth soup) for an authentic and affordable first meal (~$8–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your speedboat or shared dhoni transfer from the airport to save significantly. Shared transfers can cost as little as $20–$40 vs. $150+ for private. Confirm transfer timing with your guesthouse before arrival. Carry some USD cash as many local island vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for your first snorkeling session right off the guesthouse beach or house reef. Most boutique guesthouses in North Malé Atoll offer free or low-cost snorkel gear rental ($3–$5). Explore the colorful coral gardens and spot reef fish, sea turtles, and possibly a reef shark. Snorkel for 1.5–2 hours during the calm morning waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, join a budget group snorkeling excursion to a nearby snorkel spot or sandbank. Many local guesthouses organize shared group trips (4–6 people) to reduce costs. Visit a famous nearby snorkel point such as Banana Reef or a local coral garden. Enjoy the stunning turquoise waters and abundant marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Return by late afternoon. Rinse off and relax on the beach. Watch the sunset from the beach with a cold local drink. Enjoy a romantic beachside dinner — many guesthouses offer a simple candlelit beach dinner setup for couples at a modest extra cost.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — roshi (flatbread) with egg and tea, a classic Maldivian morning meal (~$5–$8 included or low cost)
meals.lunch: Light local lunch at a nearby tea shop (sai hotel) — short eats like bajiya (fish pastry) and samosa with tea (~$3–$5)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse beach dinner or local restaurant — grilled fish with rice and curry (~$10–$18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Always apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. Bring a reusable water bottle. Morning snorkeling offers the clearest visibility. Ask your guesthouse host for the best free snorkel spots accessible by foot or short swim.

day_by_day.morning: Maldivian Cooking Class & Local Island Cultural Tour — join this featured experience! Visit a nearby local inhabited island by dhoni boat. Walk through the island village, observe traditional Maldivian architecture, visit the local mosque (dress modestly), and browse handmade lacquerwork and woven crafts at local workshops. Learn about Maldivian history and daily island life far beyond the resort bubble.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in the hands-on Maldivian cooking class with a local family or community kitchen. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as Mas Huni, Garudhiya fish soup, Rihaakuru (fish paste), and coconut-based curries. Cook and then enjoy the meal you prepared together — a wonderfully romantic and authentic shared experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your guesthouse by boat in the late afternoon. Relax and share your cooking experience over sunset cocktails (non-alcoholic options widely available on local islands). Light evening walk on the beach under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — coconut pancakes or roshi with jam and tea
meals.lunch: Included as part of the cooking class experience — the meal you prepared yourself!
meals.dinner: Back at the guesthouse or a local restaurant — keep it light after the big cooking class lunch. Try a fresh fruit platter and grilled seafood (~$8–$12)

day_by_day.notes: The Maldivian Cooking Class & Cultural Tour typically costs $30–$60 per person when booked through local guesthouses — much cheaper than resort-organized versions. Dress modestly for the local island visit (cover shoulders and knees). This is one of the most memorable and budget-friendly cultural experiences available in the Maldives.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning dolphin watching cruise — book a shared group sunrise dolphin spotting dhoni trip. North Malé Atoll is famous for spinner dolphins that leap and play in the bow waves of boats at dawn. This is a magical, romantic experience at a budget-friendly shared group rate ($15–$25 per person). Bring your camera!
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from dolphin cruise and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the guesthouse. Relax in a hammock or on a sun lounger. Optional: rent a kayak or paddleboard from the guesthouse ($5–$10/hour) and paddle around the lagoon. Explore the shallow sandbar near the island if accessible.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic sunset picnic on the beach — prepare a simple spread with local fruits, snacks, and juices purchased from a local shop. Watch the sky turn pink and orange over the Indian Ocean. Dine at a local restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before dolphin cruise — bread, fruit, and tea
meals.lunch: Local tea shop short eats or guesthouse light lunch — fish rolls, samosas, and fresh coconut water (~$4–$6)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant dinner — whole grilled reef fish with steamed rice and coconut curry (~$12–$18)

day_by_day.notes: Book the dolphin cruise the evening before through your guesthouse to secure spots. Shared group boats are far more economical than private charters. Bring a light jacket for the early morning boat ride as it can be breezy on the water.

day_by_day.morning: House reef snorkeling session at dawn — the early morning light creates incredible underwater visibility and the reef is most active. Spend 1–2 hours exploring the house reef independently with rented gear. Look for octopus, moray eels, parrotfish, and if lucky, a reef shark or turtle resting on the sandy bottom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day trip to a nearby uninhabited sandbank (sandbankpicnic island). Many guesthouses organize shared group sandbank trips ($20–$35 per person including snorkeling stop). Spend time swimming in crystal-clear shallow water, sunbathing on pure white sand, and snorkeling around the sandbank's edge. A quintessential Maldives bucket-list experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the sandbank or back at the guesthouse beach. Enjoy a romantic evening stroll. Try stargazing — the Maldives has some of the clearest, darkest skies in the world, perfect for spotting constellations.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — egg roshi, fresh papaya, and Maldivian black tea
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch from the guesthouse or local shop for the sandbank trip — sandwiches, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Guesthouse BBQ night (many guesthouses do Friday night BBQ with fresh catch) or local restaurant (~$10–$15)

day_by_day.notes: Apply generous reef-safe sunscreen on sandbank trips — there is zero shade on open sandbars and the equatorial sun is intense. Bring a hat, sunglasses, and plenty of water. Friday is a special day in the Maldives (Islamic holy day) — some local shops may have reduced hours.

day_by_day.morning: Relax and recharge with a slow morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and take a gentle swim in the lagoon. Optional: morning yoga on the beach (some guesthouses offer free or low-cost yoga sessions). Read a book in a hammock and enjoy the peaceful island atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local island on foot or by bicycle (bike rental ~$5–$8/day). Visit local shops for handmade souvenirs — lacquerwork boxes, woven mats, and local spices make great affordable gifts. Chat with locals and learn about island life. Visit the local harbor to watch traditional dhoni fishing boats come and go.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange a private romantic beach setup with your guesthouse — many budget guesthouses will set up a simple candlelit table on the beach for couples at minimal or no extra charge. Enjoy a special dinner under the stars with the sound of gentle waves.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely guesthouse breakfast — coconut roshi, boiled egg, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Local tea house lunch — hearty Maldivian curry with rice (~$5–$8)
meals.dinner: Romantic candlelit beach dinner at the guesthouse — fresh grilled lobster or fish (splurge slightly, ~$20–$30 for two as a special treat)

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to treat yourselves to a small splurge on a romantic beach dinner since you've been saving on other days. Ask your guesthouse host to arrange it — they are usually very accommodating and it costs far less than a resort equivalent.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling trip to a famous North Malé Atoll snorkel site. Options include Manta Point (seasonal), HP Reef (Blue Canyon), or Nassimo Thila — some of the best snorkeling and diving sites in the world. Shared group snorkel trips are very affordable ($25–$40 per person). Look for manta rays, eagle rays, and large schools of fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning snorkel excursion, return to the guesthouse for lunch and a relaxing afternoon. Optional: try a budget-friendly traditional Maldivian massage offered by some local guesthouses ($20–$40 for 60 minutes — much cheaper than resort spas). Rest and rejuvenate.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dhoni cruise — a romantic shared sunset boat trip around the atoll ($15–$25 per person). Watch the sun dip below the horizon from the water with a juice or mocktail in hand. Return for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before snorkel trip — fruit, toast, and tea
meals.lunch: Guesthouse lunch — tuna curry with steamed rice and salad (~$8–$10)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant dinner — mixed seafood plate with vegetables and rice (~$12–$16)

day_by_day.notes: Manta Point visits are seasonal (best November–April, so March should be ideal!). Confirm with your guesthouse the day before about manta ray sightings. Always listen to the boat guide's safety briefing and maintain a respectful distance from marine life.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Malé city — take a shared speedboat or public ferry to the Maldivian capital (ferry is very cheap, ~$1–$2 one way). Explore the colorful and vibrant capital: visit the Grand Friday Mosque (Masjid-al-Sultan Muhammad Thakurufaanu Al Auzam), the historic Hukuru Miskiy (Old Friday Mosque built in 1656), and the National Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Malé: browse the local fish market (a fascinating and photogenic local experience), visit the fruit and vegetable market, and explore the busy streets lined with shops. Pick up affordable Maldivian souvenirs — dried fish, local spices, and handicrafts are very cheap here compared to resort shops. Walk along the Malé waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Malé at a local restaurant before the return ferry/speedboat. Malé has excellent local eateries that are far cheaper than island restaurants. Return to your guesthouse by evening speedboat.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Local Malé restaurant — traditional Maldivian rice and curry plate at a local 'sai hotel' (~$3–$6, some of the cheapest and most authentic food in the country)
meals.dinner: Malé local restaurant before return — fresh tuna steak, grilled chicken, or curry with roshi (~$6–$10)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly in Malé (cover shoulders and knees out of respect for Islamic culture). The public ferry schedule is fixed — check times with your guesthouse and plan your return accordingly. Malé is very walkable — no need for taxis within the city center.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and leisure morning after the Malé day trip. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a morning swim. Explore the guesthouse's snorkel trail at your own pace. Optional: take an underwater photography session if you have a waterproof camera or phone case — the house reef offers excellent photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Bioluminescent plankton evening preparation — spend the afternoon relaxing and napping so you can stay up late for the bioluminescent beach experience tonight. Optional afternoon activity: visit a local artisan workshop to see traditional Maldivian crafts being made — lacquerwork (liye laajehun) is a centuries-old art form.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent plankton beach experience — after dark (around 9–10 PM), walk to the beach and wade into the shallow water to witness the magical blue glowing plankton (phytoplankton). Wave your hands through the water and watch it light up. This natural phenomenon is free and one of the most romantic and unforgettable experiences in the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely guesthouse breakfast — fresh fruit platter, coconut pancakes, and tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the guesthouse or local café — tuna sandwich and fresh coconut water (~$5–$7)
meals.dinner: Early dinner at the guesthouse before the late night beach activity — grilled fish with rice and curry (~$10–$14)

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescent plankton is most visible during new moon phases when the sky is darkest. Check the lunar calendar for March 2027 — if it aligns, this will be absolutely spectacular. Ask your guesthouse host which beach spots have the most reliable plankton activity. No special equipment or cost needed — it's completely free!

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise snorkeling session — wake up just before dawn and snorkel during the magical golden hour sunrise. The early morning light filtering through the water creates extraordinary visibility and color. Look for sleeping reef sharks and resting sea turtles. A deeply peaceful and romantic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group fishing trip — traditional Maldivian hand-line fishing on a local dhoni ($20–$35 per person for a 3-hour shared trip). Learn traditional fishing techniques from local fishermen. Any fish you catch can often be prepared by the guesthouse kitchen for dinner — a truly farm-to-table experience!
day_by_day.evening: Cook your catch! Arrange with the guesthouse kitchen to prepare the fish you caught during the afternoon trip. Enjoy a romantic private dinner featuring your own freshly caught fish, grilled with local spices and served with rice and curry. A unique and memorable dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Very light pre-snorkel breakfast — banana and tea
meals.lunch: Post-fishing trip lunch at the guesthouse — light curry and roshi (~$6–$9)
meals.dinner: Your freshly caught fish dinner prepared by the guesthouse kitchen — small cooking fee (~$5–$10) plus the joy of eating what you caught!

day_by_day.notes: Traditional Maldivian hand-line fishing is done at dusk or dawn for best results, but afternoon trips are also popular. Fishing is deeply embedded in Maldivian culture and this is a fantastic way to connect with local traditions. Bring motion sickness tablets if you're sensitive to boat movement.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day snorkel and island hopping adventure — the most comprehensive snorkel experience of the trip. Book a shared group full-day island hopping and snorkeling tour ($40–$65 per person) visiting 3–4 different snorkel spots, a sandbank, and a local island. This is the best value snorkel experience available and covers the greatest variety of marine environments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continuation of the island hopping tour — visit a second and third snorkel site. Possible highlights include coral gardens, a shipwreck snorkel, turtle cleaning stations, and a nurse shark feeding area. Enjoy a packed lunch on a sandbank.
day_by_day.evening: Return to guesthouse tired and exhilarated. Rinse off and relax. Enjoy a quiet, romantic evening on the beach. Reflect on the incredible marine life witnessed throughout the day over a sunset drink.

meals.breakfast: Early guesthouse breakfast — energy-rich meal before the full day: eggs, roshi, fruit
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included in the island hopping tour or brought from the guesthouse — sandwiches, fruit, and water on the sandbank
meals.dinner: Light guesthouse dinner — fresh salad, soup, and grilled vegetables with fish (~$8–$12)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most activity-packed day of the trip — wear reef-safe SPF50+ sunscreen and reapply every 2 hours. Stay hydrated throughout the day. Bring a dry bag for your phone and valuables on the boat. This full-day tour offers the best snorkeling value for money in the entire itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisure morning — take one last long snorkel on the house reef. Say goodbye to the fish, turtles, and coral you've come to recognize over the past 12 days. Take photos and videos to remember the underwater world. Collect any remaining souvenirs from local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed afternoon of beach time, swimming, and reading. Optional: take a final kayak or paddleboard session on the lagoon. Start packing your bags. Visit any local shops for last-minute gifts — dried Maldivian tuna (rihaakuru), local honey, or handmade crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell romantic dinner — splurge slightly on your last night for a memorable meal. Request a special beach setup from the guesthouse if possible. Toast to your incredible Maldivian adventure with fresh fruit mocktails. Watch your final Maldivian sunset together.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — coconut roshi, fresh fruit, and Maldivian tea
meals.lunch: Local tea shop final visit — enjoy one last round of short eats: bajiya, gulha (fish balls), and keemia (~$4–$6)
meals.dinner: Special farewell beach dinner — grilled lobster or whole reef fish with coconut rice and local dessert (bondi or foni boakibaa cake) (~$25–$40 for two as a final splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure transfer for tomorrow morning with the guesthouse tonight. Settle any outstanding bills. Leave a review for your guesthouse — budget guesthouses rely heavily on positive reviews. Pack snorkel gear carefully if you purchased any. Keep departure documents easily accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise on the beach — sit quietly together and soak in the last moments of your Maldivian paradise. Take final photos of the turquoise lagoon, white sand, and swaying palms. Enjoy a final guesthouse breakfast. Check out and arrange transfer back to Velana International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. Browse duty-free shops for any last souvenirs. Reflect on 13 incredible days of snorkeling, romance, local culture, and natural beauty in one of the world's most stunning destinations.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry beautiful memories of the Maldives — the bioluminescent beach, dolphin sunrises, underwater coral gardens, cooking classes, and romantic beach dinners — all experienced on a genuine budget without sacrificing the magic of this extraordinary destination.

meals.breakfast: Final guesthouse breakfast — make it special: order everything you loved over the past 12 days
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — budget meal before departure (~$8–$15)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dinner depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: A well-planned 13-day Maldives trip staying in local guesthouse accommodation (North Malé Atoll) can be achieved for approximately $80–$130 per person per day including accommodation, meals, and activities — compared to $500–$2000+ per day at a resort. The experience of authentic local island life, incredible snorkeling, and genuine Maldivian culture can be equally magical at a fraction of the resort cost. Total estimated budget for two people: $2,000–$3,400 excluding international flights.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your resort transfer representative. Board a speedboat transfer to your boutique stay in North Malé Atoll (around Veligandu or Baros Island — approx. 30–45 min ride). Check in, receive a welcome drink and cool towel, and settle into your overwater or beach villa. Take a slow, unhurried stroll along the resort beach to get your bearings and soak in your first Maldivian sunset views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's main restaurant. Toast to the beginning of your honeymoon with a complimentary glass of sparkling wine (often offered to honeymooners — confirm at check-in). Watch the stars emerge over the Indian Ocean from your villa deck.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at the airport or during transfer
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant — set menu or à la carte; budget approx. $60–90 per couple for a mid-range resort dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Request honeymoon amenities (rose petals, fruit basket, sparkling wine) at check-in if not pre-arranged. Keep the evening light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the resort concierge tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up to your first full Maldivian morning. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast with ocean views. After breakfast, spend time exploring the resort island on foot — discover the house reef from the beach, spot reef fish in the shallows, and photograph the iconic turquoise lagoon. Pack your snorkel gear for a self-guided shallow-water snorkel along the resort's designated house reef entry point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book a guided house reef snorkel session with the resort's dive/water sports center (approx. $20–30 per person). An instructor will point out key marine life including parrotfish, clownfish, and sea turtles if lucky. Afterward, relax on your villa deck or a sun lounger with a tropical fruit juice. Optional: visit the resort spa for a 60-minute couple's massage (book in advance; approx. $120–160 for two).
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise — Embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden dhoni decorated with flowers and candles. Sail into the golden sunset with your partner, sipping champagne or fresh juice as the sky turns shades of orange and pink. This intimate experience is perfect for your honeymoon and typically lasts 60–90 minutes.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — included in most mid-range packages; enjoy tropical fruits, eggs, pastries, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Beach grill or sandbar café at the resort — grilled fish sandwich, fresh salad, coconut water; approx. $25–40 per couple
meals.dinner: Casual dining at the resort's beachside restaurant after the dhoni cruise — grilled seafood platter or Maldivian fish curry; approx. $55–75 per couple

day_by_day.notes: Book the Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise through the resort concierge at least 24 hours in advance. Bring a light wrap for the boat as sea breezes can feel cool after sunset. Apply reef-safe sunscreen — mandatory at most Maldivian resorts and essential for protecting the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga or meditation session on the beach or your villa deck as the sun rises (many resorts offer complimentary or low-cost sunrise yoga; check with concierge). Follow with a nourishing breakfast. Then join the Coral Garden Snorkeling Safari — a guided excursion by boat to some of North Malé Atoll's most vibrant reef systems. Drift through kaleidoscopic coral gardens teeming with reef sharks, manta rays (seasonal), eagle rays, and hundreds of tropical fish species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the snorkeling safari by midday. Rinse off and enjoy a leisurely lunch. Spend the afternoon at leisure — read on the beach, float in the lagoon, or explore the resort's water sports offerings (kayaking, paddleboarding, or glass-bottom boat rides are typically available at mid-range resorts for $15–30 per activity).
day_by_day.evening: Romantic dinner for two at the resort's specialty restaurant or a private beach dining setup (pre-book with concierge; a private beach dinner typically costs $80–150 per couple at a mid-range boutique resort and is absolutely worth it for honeymooners). Dine under the stars with the sound of waves as your soundtrack.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — fuel up well before the snorkeling safari
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — fresh wraps, tropical smoothies, or a mezze platter; approx. $20–35 per couple
meals.dinner: Private beach dining or specialty restaurant — fresh lobster, grilled mahi-mahi, or Maldivian mas huni (tuna salad); approx. $70–110 per couple

day_by_day.notes: The Coral Garden Snorkeling Safari typically runs 3–4 hours and covers 2–3 snorkeling spots. Wear a rash guard for sun protection during extended time in the water. Bring an underwater camera or rent a GoPro from the dive center to capture memories.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent morning — breakfast in bed or on your villa deck if your accommodation offers this (request the night before). Head to the resort spa for a couple's treatment: a traditional Maldivian body scrub using coconut and local herbs followed by a 45-minute relaxation massage. This is a deeply romantic and rejuvenating experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the spa, change into swimwear and head to the lagoon for a relaxed afternoon of swimming and snorkeling independently along the house reef. Look out for sea turtles, which are commonly spotted in North Malé Atoll. Alternatively, rent a kayak and paddle around the island perimeter for gentle exercise and beautiful perspectives of your resort island.
day_by_day.evening: Maldivian Cooking Class & Local Island Cultural Tour — In the late afternoon/early evening, take a short speedboat ride to a nearby local inhabited island. Experience authentic Maldivian village life, visit local homes, a mosque, and a fishing harbor. Participate in a hands-on cooking class learning to prepare traditional dishes like garudhiya (fish broth), roshi (flatbread), and coconut-based curries. Return to the resort by 20:00.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast or resort buffet — fresh tropical fruits, Maldivian roshi with coconut sambal, eggs
meals.lunch: Pool-side lunch at the resort — fish tacos, fresh salad, iced coffee; approx. $25–40 per couple
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as part of the cultural tour experience, or dine at the resort's main restaurant upon return; approx. $50–70 per couple

day_by_day.notes: The local island cultural tour typically lasts 3–4 hours and costs approx. $50–80 per person through the resort. Dress modestly for the local island visit (cover shoulders and knees out of respect for local Islamic customs). This is one of the most enriching experiences in the Maldives — don't skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling session at a different spot along the house reef or a short boat ride to a nearby reef. Focus on spotting different species than Day 3 — ask your dive center staff for recommendations based on tides and visibility. After snorkeling, enjoy a refreshing outdoor shower and relax with a book in a hammock or on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on a sandbank excursion — a quintessential Maldivian experience. Your resort can arrange a speedboat trip to a nearby uninhabited sandbank (tiny strip of white sand in the middle of the turquoise ocean). Bring a picnic lunch, snorkel, and a camera. You'll feel like you have the entire ocean to yourselves. Duration: 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Beach Night Walk — After dark, head to the beach for the magical natural phenomenon of bioluminescent plankton lighting up the shoreline with electric blue light. Walk barefoot along the water's edge and watch the waves glow with each crash. This ethereal experience is most vivid on darker nights away from resort lighting. Pair it with a nightcap on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — eggs Benedict, tropical fruit platters, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Picnic basket on the sandbank — pre-order from the resort the night before; typically includes sandwiches, fruit, chips, and cold drinks; approx. $30–50 per couple
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort's beach bar or grill — wood-fired pizza, grilled catch of the day, craft cocktails; approx. $50–70 per couple

day_by_day.notes: The bioluminescent plankton phenomenon (Noctiluca scintillans) is most visible between July and February but can sometimes be seen year-round in the Maldives. March sightings are possible — ask the resort staff about recent activity. The sandbank excursion costs approx. $30–60 per couple and should be booked a day ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and relaxation morning. Sleep in, enjoy breakfast at a leisurely pace, and spend the morning floating in the lagoon or reading on your villa deck. This is a 'slow day' intentionally built into your itinerary to avoid activity fatigue and truly savor the Maldivian pace of life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the resort's water sports center and try something new — stand-up paddleboarding (SUP), windsurfing beginner lesson, or a glass-bottom kayak tour of the lagoon. These activities typically cost $15–40 per hour at mid-range resorts. Afterward, enjoy a late afternoon swim and watch the changing colors of the lagoon as the sun moves lower.
day_by_day.evening: Underwater Restaurant Dinner for Two — This is the crown jewel of your dining experiences. Descend into an all-glass underwater restaurant (available at select resorts in North Malé Atoll or accessible by short transfer) and dine surrounded by the living ocean. Watch reef fish, rays, and sharks glide past as you enjoy a curated tasting menu of fresh seafood and international cuisine. This is an unforgettable, once-in-a-lifetime honeymoon dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — slow and indulgent; try the Maldivian-style breakfast with tuna curry and roshi
meals.lunch: Light poolside snack — fresh fruit platter, hummus and pita, sparkling water; approx. $15–25 per couple
meals.dinner: Underwater restaurant — prix fixe tasting menu typically costs $150–250 per couple; book well in advance as tables are extremely limited. This is a splurge worth every cent for a honeymoon.

day_by_day.notes: The underwater restaurant experience may require a short speedboat transfer to a neighboring resort if your accommodation doesn't have one on-site — coordinate with your concierge. Book this at least 3–5 days in advance. Dress code is usually smart-casual (no swimwear). This is your most expensive dinner — budget accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint of your trip — celebrate with a sunrise swim in the lagoon before anyone else is awake. Afterward, join the resort's complimentary guided snorkel tour of the house reef (many resorts offer this daily at no extra charge). Focus on coral identification and marine life spotting with a knowledgeable guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the resort's spa for individual treatments — choose from a selection of massages, facials, or body wraps. A 60-minute hot stone massage or a Balinese massage is highly recommended. Rest afterward in the spa's relaxation area with herbal tea and cool towels. Spend the remaining afternoon at the beach, collecting shells and simply being present.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise (second experience, different route or theme) — If your first dhoni cruise was so magical you want to repeat it, book again with a different setup (perhaps a stargazing dhoni cruise after sunset, with the crew pointing out constellations over the Indian Ocean). Alternatively, enjoy cocktails at the resort's overwater bar as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — eggs any style, fresh pastries, tropical smoothie bowl
meals.lunch: Resort restaurant — Maldivian fish soup, grilled tuna steak with coconut rice; approx. $35–55 per couple
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant — romantic table for two on the sand, fresh seafood barbecue night (many resorts host this on weekends); approx. $60–85 per couple

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is your halfway point — use today to reflect on your favorite experiences so far and confirm any remaining activity bookings for the second half of the trip. Consider purchasing a reef-safe sunscreen refill from the resort shop if running low.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a dolphin-watching boat excursion — North Malé Atoll is one of the best places in the world to spot spinner dolphins in the wild. Many resorts offer early morning dolphin cruises (06:30–08:30) as the dolphins are most active at dawn. Return for a late breakfast full of excitement and stories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Coral Garden Snorkeling Safari (second session, different reef site) — Return to the water for another guided snorkeling safari, this time exploring a different coral garden system. Your guide will take you to spots known for specific marine life — nurse sharks resting on the sandy bottom, schools of fusiliers, and vibrant hard coral formations. This is Maldives snorkeling at its finest.
day_by_day.evening: Low-key evening at the resort. Enjoy sundowners at the overwater bar, then have dinner at the resort's casual dining venue. Spend the night stargazing from your villa deck — the Maldives has some of the least light-polluted skies in Asia, and the Milky Way is often visible with the naked eye.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast after dolphin cruise — resort buffet or à la carte eggs, fresh juice, coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the dive center café or beach grill — fish burger, coleslaw, iced tea; approx. $20–35 per couple
meals.dinner: Casual resort dining — pasta with fresh seafood, wood-fired flatbreads, local desserts like bondi (Maldivian sweet); approx. $45–65 per couple

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin-watching excursions typically cost $30–50 per person and last 2 hours. Spinner dolphins are common in North Malé Atoll year-round. Bring a telephoto lens or zoom camera for dolphin photography. The second snorkeling safari can be booked as a half-day trip (approx. $40–60 per person with guide and equipment).

day_by_day.morning: Full morning of leisure and romance. Breakfast in bed (pre-order from room service the night before — a mid-range boutique resort typically offers this for $20–35 per couple). Afterward, spend the morning in your villa — read, connect, and simply enjoy each other's company in paradise. Take a late-morning dip in your villa's private plunge pool if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the resort island more deeply — visit the resort's marine biology station or coral nursery if available (many eco-conscious resorts in the Maldives run coral restoration programs and welcome guests to learn and participate). This is a meaningful, educational, and romantic activity. Alternatively, join a glass-bottom boat tour of the lagoon to observe marine life without getting wet.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Beach Night Walk (second attempt if the first was not optimal, or a longer exploration) — Head to the darkest part of the beach after 21:00 for the best chance of seeing glowing plankton. Bring a blanket and lie on the sand afterward to stargaze together. This is one of the most romantic and naturally magical experiences the Maldives offers.

meals.breakfast: In-villa room service breakfast — continental spread with local fruits, yogurt, pastries, coffee
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar — fresh salads, cold sandwiches, tropical fruit juices; approx. $25–40 per couple
meals.dinner: Resort specialty restaurant — Asian fusion or Mediterranean menu; fresh tuna sashimi, grilled octopus, mango sorbet; approx. $65–90 per couple

day_by_day.notes: If your resort has a coral restoration program, participation is usually free or at a nominal cost and is a deeply memorable experience. Ask the concierge about the marine biology team's schedule. For the bioluminescence walk, allow your eyes 10–15 minutes to adjust to the darkness before expecting to see the glow.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at a new spot — ask the dive center about the best current reef conditions and request a guided trip to a channel or drift snorkel site. Drift snorkeling (letting the current carry you over a reef) is an exhilarating experience and requires a guide. You may encounter grey reef sharks, turtles, and large pelagic fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return and have lunch, then spend the afternoon taking a beginner scuba diving discovery course (Discover Scuba Diving) if you haven't dived before. This 2–3 hour experience includes a pool session and a shallow open-water dive to 5–8 meters. It's a transformative experience that opens up a whole new underwater world. Cost: approx. $80–120 per person at most Maldivian resort dive centers.
day_by_day.evening: Maldivian Cooking Class (second session or alternative local experience) — If you missed Day 4's cultural tour or want more culinary depth, arrange an evening cooking class at the resort with the head chef. Learn to make traditional Maldivian sweets, fresh coconut sambal, and the iconic Maldivian short eats (hedhikaa) — perfect for recreating memories at home.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — hearty breakfast before the active morning; eggs, fresh fruit, granola, coffee
meals.lunch: Post-snorkel lunch at the beach grill — grilled fish wrap, fresh coconut water, tropical fruit; approx. $25–40 per couple
meals.dinner: Enjoy dishes from the cooking class, or dine at the resort's main restaurant — Maldivian curry night; approx. $50–70 per couple

day_by_day.notes: The Discover Scuba Diving experience does not require a certification and is suitable for anyone in good health. Inform the dive instructor of any medical conditions beforehand. Drift snorkeling should only be done with a certified guide due to current variability. Both activities should be booked the previous day.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, peaceful morning — your second-to-last full day in paradise. Wake up early to watch the sunrise from the beach or your villa deck (sunrise in the Maldives in March is around 06:10). Enjoy a long breakfast and then spend the morning writing postcards, journaling, or simply sitting with your feet in the sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final snorkeling session — revisit your favorite reef spot from the trip for one last underwater adventure. Take your time and say goodbye to the coral gardens, the fish, and the turtles that have become familiar friends over the past week. Afterward, visit the resort boutique to pick up souvenirs — local crafts, reef-safe sunscreen, or Maldivian spices and tea.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise (final, most romantic version) — Book a special sunset dhoni experience for your last full evening, perhaps with a private chef preparing canapes on board, or a musician playing traditional Maldivian bodu beru drums. Watch the sun sink into the Indian Ocean one final time from the water. This is your farewell to paradise.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — take your time and savor every bite knowing it's one of your last mornings here
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the overwater bar — sushi rolls, fresh sashimi, sparkling water; approx. $35–55 per couple
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — pre-arrange a romantic table setup with the concierge (candles, flowers, personalized menu); approx. $90–130 per couple

day_by_day.notes: Ask the resort to arrange a special farewell dinner setup — many resorts do this complimentarily for honeymooners or at a small decoration fee. Pack non-essential items tonight to make departure day easier. Confirm your departure transfer time and luggage pickup with the front desk.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Maldives. Wake up early for one last sunrise swim in the lagoon — just the two of you. Enjoy a final breakfast with all your favorite items from the buffet. Check out of your villa (standard checkout is usually 12:00 noon, though many resorts offer late checkout until 14:00–16:00 for an additional fee — worth requesting for honeymooners).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your remaining hours at the resort's day-use facilities (pool, beach, spa lounge) if late checkout was granted. Take final photos of the resort, the lagoon, and each other. At the designated time, board your speedboat transfer back to Velana International Airport. Arrive with 2–3 hours before your departure flight. Browse duty-free for Maldivian souvenirs, local honey, or handicrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Velana International Airport. Carry your memories, your tan, and the glow of your honeymoon with you as you fly home. The Indian Ocean will always be waiting for your return.

meals.breakfast: Final resort buffet — make it special; order a mimosa or fresh juice cocktail to celebrate
meals.lunch: Light meal at the resort before checkout, or at the airport — Maldivian short eats (bajiya, gulha) from an airport café; approx. $15–25 per couple
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at your layover destination

day_by_day.notes: Late checkout (until 16:00) typically costs $50–100 extra but is highly recommended to avoid spending hours at the airport. Confirm transfer timing carefully — speedboat transfers must be timed precisely with tides and flight schedules. Leave a glowing review for the resort and tip your favorite staff members — it means the world to them.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — depending on your flight routing (via Dubai, Doha, Colombo, or Singapore), you may arrive home today or tomorrow. If you have a long layover in a hub city, consider booking a day-use hotel room near the airport for a shower, rest, and a proper meal before your connecting flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue homeward journey. Use travel time to organize your photos, share highlights with family and friends, and begin planning your next Maldives adventure — because one visit is never enough.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive home. Unpack your shells, your sarongs, and your stories. Recreate a Maldivian dinner at home using the recipes from your cooking class — coconut fish curry and roshi — and toast to an unforgettable honeymoon.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or layover airport meal
meals.lunch: In-flight or layover restaurant
meals.dinner: Home-cooked Maldivian meal using recipes from your cooking class, or a celebratory dinner at your favorite local restaurant

day_by_day.notes: This final day is a buffer/travel day built into the itinerary to account for long-haul flight durations from the Maldives to most European or American destinations. Flight LH likely routes through a Middle Eastern or Asian hub. Carry all valuables, cameras, and memory cards in your carry-on luggage. Welcome home — and congratulations on your honeymoon!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Maldives Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, around Veligandu or Baros Island Boutique Stay
hotel.location: North Malé Atoll, around Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise
experiences.description: Embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden boat (dhoni) decorated with flowers and candles for a private sunset cruise with your partner. Enjoy champagne, fresh tropical fruits, and canapés while watching the sky turn shades of gold and pink over the Indian Ocean. A quintessential romantic honeymoon experience unique to the Maldives.
experiences.location: North Malé Atoll, around Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Coral Garden Snorkeling Safari
experiences.description: Explore some of the most vibrant coral reefs in the world on a guided snorkeling safari. Drift through kaleidoscopic coral gardens teeming with sea turtles, reef sharks, manta rays, and thousands of tropical fish. A professional guide leads you to three different snorkeling spots across the atoll, including a famous manta ray cleaning station.
experiences.location: Hanifaru Bay, Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve

experiences.name: Underwater Restaurant Dinner for Two
experiences.description: Dine in an extraordinary all-glass underwater restaurant surrounded by the living ocean. Enjoy a curated five-course fine dining menu featuring fresh Maldivian lobster, tuna sashimi, and decadent desserts while nurse sharks and colorful reef fish glide past your table. An unforgettable luxury dining experience perfect for honeymooners.
experiences.location: Ithaa Undersea Restaurant, Conrad Maldives Rangali Island, South Ari Atoll

experiences.name: Bioluminescent Beach Night Walk
experiences.description: After dark, witness the magical natural phenomenon of bioluminescent plankton lighting up the shoreline in electric blue as waves wash ashore. Walk hand-in-hand along the beach as the water glows beneath your feet. Combine this with a private stargazing session guided by a resort astronomer using high-powered telescopes under some of the clearest skies on Earth.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class & Local Island Cultural Tour
experiences.description: Visit a local inhabited island to experience authentic Maldivian culture beyond the resort bubble. Tour a traditional fishing village, visit a local mosque, and browse handcrafted lacquerware at a artisan workshop. Then join a hands-on cooking class learning to prepare classic dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut), garudhiya fish soup, and coconut roshi flatbread using fresh local ingredients.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect luggage, then meet your private resort transfer coordinator. Board a luxury speedboat or seaplane transfer to your boutique resort in North Malé Atoll (Veligandu or Baros area). Check in to your overwater villa or beach bungalow, enjoy a chilled welcome mocktail/cocktail and a cold towel ceremony. Take a leisurely orientation stroll around the resort grounds and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise — embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden dhoni decorated with tropical flowers and candles. Drift across the glassy lagoon as the sun melts into the Indian Ocean horizon. Sip champagne and enjoy canapés prepared by your resort chef while the sky turns shades of amber and rose.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread served in your villa upon arrival — fresh tropical fruit platter, Maldivian short eats (bajiya, gulha), and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Romantic à la carte dinner at the resort's signature overwater restaurant — choose from fresh catch of the day, lobster thermidor, or pan-seared sea bass paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Ensure resort transfer is pre-arranged before arrival. Confirm villa type (overwater bungalow recommended for honeymoon). Request rose petal turndown service and a bottle of champagne on ice for arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up to a private in-villa breakfast served on your deck overlooking the lagoon. After breakfast, enjoy a guided house reef snorkeling session directly from the resort jetty. Explore the coral garden teeming with parrotfish, hawksbill turtles, and vibrant reef fish — fins, masks, and guides provided by the resort's marine biologist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Coral Garden Snorkeling Safari — board a resort dhoni and head to the most pristine coral reef systems in North Malé Atoll. Drift snorkel through kaleidoscopic coral gardens, spot nurse sharks resting on sandy patches, and swim alongside manta rays if in season. The marine guide provides expert commentary on reef ecology.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Beach Night Walk — after dark, stroll along the shoreline and witness the magical blue glow of bioluminescent plankton lighting up the waves with every step. Your resort naturalist guide explains the science behind this ethereal phenomenon. Return to the villa for a private stargazing session from your deck.

meals.breakfast: Private in-villa breakfast — eggs benedict, fresh-squeezed tropical juices, pastries, and a Maldivian fish curry side
meals.lunch: Casual beachside grill lunch — grilled reef fish tacos, coconut prawn skewers, and a fresh mango salad at the resort's beach shack
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner for two on the beach — private table set directly on the sand with tiki torches, a five-course tasting menu featuring Maldivian and Mediterranean fusion

day_by_day.notes: Book the Bioluminescent Beach Night Walk in advance through the resort activities desk. Best experienced on a new moon night — check lunar calendar. Bring waterproof sandals for the night walk.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a sunrise yoga session on your overwater villa deck or at the resort's open-air yoga pavilion facing the ocean. Follow with a couples' spa treatment at the resort's water bungalow spa — choose from a traditional Maldivian coconut oil massage or a hot stone therapy session with ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maldivian Cooking Class & Local Island Cultural Tour — board a resort speedboat and visit a nearby local inhabited island. Explore colorful streets, visit the Friday mosque, browse local craft stalls, and interact with friendly islanders. Then join a Maldivian cooking class: learn to prepare garudhiya (tuna broth), mas huni (tuna and coconut), and coconut roshi flatbread with a local family.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy sundowners at the resort's over-lagoon bar. As night falls, dine at the resort's main restaurant — request a window table for views of the illuminated lagoon.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — live egg station, tropical fruit display, smoked fish, Maldivian hedhikaa (short eats), freshly baked breads
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class on the local island, served with fresh lime juice and palm toddy (non-alcoholic option available)
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant — pan-roasted lobster with saffron bisque, wagyu beef tenderloin, and a shared chocolate fondant dessert with raspberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: The local island cultural tour requires modest dress — bring a sarong or light cover-up. Tipping the local cooking class host is warmly appreciated. Confirm speedboat departure time the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — sleep in and enjoy a late in-villa breakfast. Spend the morning lounging on your private sun deck or dipping in the villa's plunge pool. Read, reconnect, and simply soak in the stillness of the Indian Ocean around you.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a private dolphin-watching cruise around the North Malé Atoll channels — spinner and bottlenose dolphins are commonly spotted here in the afternoons. Your private guide will navigate to known dolphin hotspots. Bring a camera for incredible close encounters.
day_by_day.evening: Underwater Restaurant Dinner for Two — descend into one of the Maldives' iconic all-glass underwater restaurants (available at nearby luxury resorts accessible by short transfer, or at your own resort if available). Dine surrounded by the living reef as reef sharks, rays, and tropical fish glide past your table. Enjoy a curated multi-course tasting menu with sommelier-paired wines.

meals.breakfast: Late in-villa breakfast — avocado toast, smoked salmon, fresh tropical fruit bowl, and a cold brew coffee or herbal tea
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — chilled gazpacho, grilled calamari, and a Caesar salad with fresh-baked focaccia
meals.dinner: Underwater Restaurant — five-course set menu featuring premium seafood: oysters, tuna tataki, lobster bisque, grilled barramundi, and a passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Underwater restaurant reservations must be made well in advance (at least 2–3 weeks before travel). Smart casual dress code applies — no flip-flops or swimwear. Confirm transfer arrangements if the restaurant is at a neighboring resort.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling at the house reef during the golden hour — the reef is most active at dawn. Look out for octopus, moray eels, and juvenile reef sharks in the shallower sandy areas near the coral heads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sandbank picnic experience — your resort sets up a luxury picnic on a secluded uninhabited sandbank accessible by a short dhoni ride. Arrive to find a beautifully laid table, chilled wine, fresh seafood, and a sun umbrella. Swim, snorkel, and beachcomb in complete privacy on your own tiny island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a couples' sunset cocktail experience at the over-lagoon bar. Watch the sun set with handcrafted cocktails — try a Maldivian Sunset (local rum, passion fruit, lime, and coconut water). Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's casual beachfront bistro.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — freshly made dosas, tropical smoothie bowls, poached eggs, and a selection of local Maldivian pastries
meals.lunch: Luxury sandbank picnic — chilled lobster, smoked salmon blinis, artisan cheeses, fresh fruit, and sparkling rosé
meals.dinner: Beachfront bistro — grilled whole snapper with lemon herb butter, truffle fries, and a shared tiramisu

day_by_day.notes: The sandbank picnic is weather-dependent — confirm with the resort the morning of. Apply high-SPF sunscreen generously as the sandbank offers limited shade. Bring a waterproof bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast in bed or on your deck. Spend time in the resort's infinity pool overlooking the lagoon. Optional: book a private snorkeling lesson or underwater photography session with the resort's dive center to improve your technique.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided snorkeling excursion to a nearby thilas (submerged coral pinnacle) — these are considered the crown jewels of Maldivian snorkeling, with dramatic overhangs covered in soft corals, schools of fusiliers, and frequent sightings of white-tip reef sharks and grey reef sharks patrolling the drop-offs.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise (second experience, different route) — this time venture toward the outer atoll edge for a more dramatic sunset backdrop. Enjoy a curated cheese and charcuterie board with champagne as the stars begin to appear. Return under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast in bed — fresh croissants, jam, butter, sliced tropical fruit, and a French press coffee
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar — club sandwich, sweet potato fries, and a fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's premium restaurant — tasting menu with wine pairing: amuse-bouche, sashimi of local yellowfin tuna, lobster ravioli, herb-crusted rack of lamb, and a dark chocolate and sea salt tart

day_by_day.notes: The thilas snorkeling site may have mild currents — confirm fitness level with the guide. Life jackets and flotation devices are available. Underwater cameras can be rented from the dive center.

day_by_day.morning: Full spa morning — indulge in an extended couples' spa journey at the resort's overwater spa. Begin with a Hammam scrub, followed by a traditional Maldivian Dhivehi massage using locally sourced coconut oil, frangipani, and turmeric. End with a shared hydrotherapy soak in a flower-petal bath.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the resort's water sports offerings — try stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking through the lagoon's calm turquoise waters, or a beginner windsurfing lesson. Alternatively, simply relax in a hammock strung between two palms on the beach with a good book.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Beach Night Walk (second evening, different beach section) — explore a longer stretch of shoreline and look for bioluminescent plankton in the wave wash and in rock pools. Your naturalist guide shares local folklore about the 'sea of stars.' End the evening with a nightcap at the over-lagoon bar.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — eggs any style, freshly baked breads, Maldivian fish curry, tropical juices, and a yogurt and granola bar
meals.lunch: Light spa-friendly lunch — açaí bowl, grilled vegetable wrap, and a fresh watermelon and mint juice
meals.dinner: Romantic in-villa dining — private chef prepares a three-course dinner on your deck: chilled prawn cocktail, grilled whole lobster with garlic butter, and a crème brûlée under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Book the couples' spa journey at least 48 hours in advance. In-villa private chef dinner requires a minimum 24-hour reservation with the resort's F&B team. Specify any dietary restrictions when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning manta ray snorkeling excursion — North Malé Atoll's cleaning stations are world-famous for manta ray aggregations. Depart at dawn for the best conditions. Snorkel above a cleaning station as mantas glide effortlessly beneath you in a mesmerizing aerial ballet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort by midday. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the resort's beach club — lounge on a private cabana with dedicated butler service, sip on fresh tropical cocktails, and take a refreshing dip in the lagoon. Optional: book a 30-minute sunset jet ski tour of the atoll.
day_by_day.evening: Underwater Restaurant Dinner (if not yet experienced, or a second visit at a different property) — alternatively, enjoy a premium BBQ night on the beach: live cooking stations featuring whole grilled lobster, Maldivian-spiced reef fish, and a dessert station with flambéed bananas foster.

meals.breakfast: Pre-excursion packed breakfast — energy bars, tropical fruit, and a thermos of coffee prepared by the resort
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — grilled prawn and mango salad, wagyu beef sliders, and a fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Beach BBQ night — whole grilled lobster, reef fish with Maldivian spice rub, grilled vegetables, rice pilaf, and a dessert station with local sweets

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray sightings are most reliable between November and April — March is an excellent month. Avoid touching or chasing mantas. The resort's marine biologist will brief you on responsible wildlife interaction.

day_by_day.morning: Coral Garden Snorkeling Safari (second excursion, different reef system) — visit a more remote coral garden farther into the atoll. This site is known for its pristine table corals, brain corals, and large Napoleon wrasse. The drift snorkel here is gentle and suitable for all levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maldivian Cooking Class Part 2 — this time, a private in-resort cooking session with the resort's head chef. Learn to prepare a full Maldivian feast: rihaakuru (tuna paste), fihunu mas (grilled fish with chili), and a traditional Maldivian sweet — bondibaiy (coconut rice pudding).
day_by_day.evening: Romantic sundowner on the private sandbank — your resort arranges a surprise evening setup: a small fire pit, floor cushions, Moroccan lanterns, and a chilled bottle of vintage champagne. Watch the Milky Way emerge as night falls over the open ocean.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast — smashed avocado with poached eggs, fresh papaya, and a cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared in the cooking class — a full Maldivian lunch spread served in the resort's garden pavilion
meals.dinner: Sandbank evening — gourmet canapés, charcuterie, artisan chocolates, and champagne under the stars (light grazing dinner format)

day_by_day.notes: The private sandbank evening setup requires advance booking (minimum 48 hours). Weather-dependent — have an in-villa backup plan arranged. Bring insect repellent for the evening outdoors.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking — paddle out into the calm lagoon at first light and watch the sun rise over the horizon in complete silence. The lagoon is mirror-flat at dawn and the colors are extraordinary. Return for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to a neighboring luxury resort for a guest experience — many North Malé Atoll resorts offer day passes that include access to their pools, beach clubs, and water sports. Explore a different island aesthetic while maintaining the luxury standard.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your resort and enjoy a private couples' cocktail masterclass with the resort's head bartender — learn to mix three signature Maldivian cocktails using local ingredients: coconut arrack, pandan syrup, and fresh tropical fruits. Enjoy your creations as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — full spread with live cooking stations, tropical fruits, and a Maldivian breakfast corner
meals.lunch: Lunch at the neighboring resort's beach club — fresh seafood platter, tropical salads, and a chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Resort's signature restaurant — chef's special tasting menu: seven courses with optional wine pairing, featuring the freshest local catch and imported premium ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Day pass to a neighboring resort must be pre-arranged and may incur an additional cost. Confirm availability and inclusions before departure. The cocktail masterclass is typically complimentary for honeymoon guests — confirm with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at complete leisure — your last full active day begins slowly. Sleep in, enjoy breakfast in bed, and spend the morning floating in your villa's plunge pool or the lagoon. Optional: book a final snorkeling session at the house reef to say goodbye to your favorite fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise (final experience) — this time, a longer sunset cruise that circumnavigates the entire atoll. Stop at a shallow sandbank for a quick swim, watch for flying fish skimming the surface, and toast to your honeymoon with a magnum of champagne as the sun descends.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent Beach Night Walk — final night walk, this time with a private guide who takes you to the most spectacular stretch of bioluminescent shoreline. Collect glowing water in your hands and watch it cascade like liquid light. A truly unforgettable farewell to the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Lavish in-villa breakfast — full English breakfast with eggs, bacon, grilled tomatoes, mushrooms, freshly squeezed juices, and pastries
meals.lunch: Beachside light lunch — fresh sashimi platter, miso soup, edamame, and a tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner — resort arranges a special honeymoon table on the beach with personalized menu, floral decorations, and a complimentary anniversary cake or dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Inform the resort it is your final evening — most luxury resorts will arrange a special farewell experience for honeymoon couples at no extra charge. Pack non-essential items this evening to ease tomorrow's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise over the Indian Ocean from your villa deck. Take a slow walk along the beach, collect a few shells as keepsakes, and soak in the last moments of your private paradise. Enjoy a final in-villa breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out formalities — settle any outstanding bills and enjoy a complimentary late checkout (confirm with resort, typically available until 14:00 for premium guests). Spend remaining time at the pool or beach. Board your luxury speedboat or seaplane transfer back to Velana International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Velana International Airport — if your flight departs in the evening, enjoy the airport's premium lounge. Browse duty-free for Maldivian souvenirs: local lacquerwork, black coral jewelry (ethically sourced), and Maldivian coffee. Board your homeward flight with memories to last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final in-villa breakfast — your choice of any item from the full breakfast menu, served on your deck one last time
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge or a final resort lunch — grilled fish and chips, tropical fruit platter, and a farewell cocktail
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dinner or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Reconfirm airport transfer timing the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for seaplane/speedboat transfer plus airport check-in. Keep travel documents, passports, and boarding passes easily accessible.

day_by_day.morning: In-flight or transit day — if the return journey involves a long-haul flight or layover, use this time to rest and reflect on an extraordinary 13 days in paradise. Review photos, write a travel journal entry, or simply sleep and recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue journey home or enjoy a layover city stopover if applicable. If transiting through a major hub (Dubai, Singapore, Doha), consider a brief city excursion or a premium airport hotel day room for a shower and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive home — carry the warmth, tranquility, and romance of the Maldives with you. Begin planning your next adventure.

meals.breakfast: In-flight premium cabin breakfast or airport lounge breakfast
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport lounge lunch
meals.dinner: In-flight or home-cooked welcome-back meal

day_by_day.notes: This day serves as a travel buffer. If your return flight lands on Day 12, this day can be used as an optional extension day at the resort or a stopover experience. Keep all resort receipts and travel documents for travel insurance records.
